taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, using only the information in the provided rules.

## 1) Single-loop path puzzles
These require drawing one continuous loop under special constraints.

- **Dotchi-Loop** — single loop; must go through all white circles; in each bold-lined area, circles must be traversed in a uniform straight/turn pattern; black circles are forbidden.
- **Masyu** — single loop; passes through all circles; white circles require straight passage plus a turn in an adjacent cell; black circles require a turn in the circle cell and straight continuation afterward.
- **Mid-loop** — single loop; must pass through all black circles, with each black circle being the midpoint of a straight segment.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — single loop; passes through each room once; each room must contain either all moon cells or all sun cells, and the type alternates from one room to the next.
- **Slitherlink** — single loop on dot grid; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell.
- **Suraromu** — single loop; must pass through gates; loop starts/ends at the open numbered circle and must visit gates in numbered order.
- **Yajilin** — single loop; black cells are placed separately; arrow numbers indicate the number of black cells in the arrow direction.
- **Nagareru** — single directed loop; must go through black-arrow cells; wind direction constrains how the loop can move.
- **Numberlink** — connect same-number pairs with non-crossing continuous lines; lines cannot pass through numbered cells.
- **Hebi** — snakes numbered 1 to 5 must be sequentially connected; not a loop, but path-based.

## 2) Region partitioning / tiling puzzles
These involve dividing the grid into blocks, rooms, rectangles, L-shapes, or other regions.

- **Chained Block** — fill black blocks; each block has a size/shape number or “?”; all blocks must form a chain by corner contact; no repeated block shapes in a chain.
- **Double Choco** — divide grid into blocks; each block contains a pair of same-shaped white and gray areas, possibly rotated/mirrored.
- **Evolomino** — draw squares so each block contains exactly one square on an arrow; arrow routes must progress by adding one square to the previous block without rotation/flipping.
- **Five Cells** — divide the grid into blocks of exactly five cells; numbers show how many block lines surround a cell.
- **Fillomino** — fill the grid into numbered blocks; each block size equals its number; same-sized blocks cannot touch.
- **Heyawake** — rooms with numbers specifying black-cell counts; black cells cannot touch; white cells have straight-line restrictions.
- **Juosan** — fill cells with horizontal/vertical marks; territories indicate counts of marks, with mark-length restrictions.
- **LITS** — place tetrominoes in each room; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch except at corners; colored cells must be connected and avoid 2×2 or larger squares.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers; each room contains 1..n; arrow cells point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Norinori** — place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares; each bold area contains two black squares.
- **Nuritwin** — shade cells so each outlined region contains exactly two blocks of equal size; all shaded cells connect across regions.
- **Pencils** — identify pencil-shaped straight groups; each block has one tip; line length matches pencil numbers.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers from 1; duplicate numbers in rows/columns must be spaced by at least their value.
- **Sashigane** — partition into one-cell-wide L-shaped blocks; open circles are bends, arrows point to the bend.
- **Shikaku** — divide the grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its area.
- **Sto-stone** — shade cells into rooms with black-cell counts; after “dropping” stones, the bottom half fills completely.
- **Sudoku** — fill cells with 1–9 so rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks each contain all digits.
- **Tilepaint** — divide into tiles; cells in a tile must all be colored or all uncolored; diagonal-number clues constrain black cells along lines.
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles in squares; remaining white cells must form a rectangle/square.
- **Choco Banana** — paint some cells black so black regions are rectangles/squares and white regions are not rectangles/squares.
- **Usowan** — shade cells; each region has exactly one wrong number; shaded cells must not touch and white cells stay connected.

## 3) Connectivity / wall / territory puzzles
These emphasize connected white or black areas, walls, or separation constraints.

- **Hitori** — blacken cells so numbers are unique in each row/column; black cells cannot touch; white cells must stay connected.
- **Kurodoko** — blacken cells; numbers indicate visible white-cell counts to the nearest black cell or border; black cells cannot touch; white cells must connect.
- **Nurikabe** — black cells form one continuous wall; numbered white islands each have size matching the number; black cannot form 2×2.
- **Nurimeizu** — paint walls to create a maze from S to G; white cells must remain connected and non-cyclic; rooms containing S/G/circle/triangle have special coloring restrictions.
- **Nurimisaki** — mark Misaki cells white; white cells form one connected network; straight-line white counts are given in circles; no 2×2 same-color blocks.
- **Hebi** — snakes must not touch; snake parts are connected sequentially; directional viewing clues constrain visibility.
- **Kurotto** — color cells so each circle clue equals the sum of continuous black cells extending from it; circles themselves stay uncolored.
- **Norinori** — black squares are placed in pairs in regions; regions require exactly two black squares.

## 4) Line-drawing / route puzzles without single-loop requirement
These involve drawing paths, but not necessarily a single closed loop.

- **Numberlink** — connect identical numbers with continuous non-crossing paths.
- **Evolomino** — arrow routes connect blocks by growth in shape/size progression.
- **Pencils** — draw lines from pencil tips through pencil cells; line length matches pencil numbers.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles through tracks into countries; paths must not cross or pass over other circles.
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas with arrow paths; each gray area’s sum must match the circles entering it.

## 5) Number-placement / arithmetic puzzles
These are primarily about placing numbers under arithmetic or ordering constraints.

- **Sudoku** — standard 1–9 placement in rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks.
- **Fillomino** — numbers determine block sizes.
- **Ripple Effect** — consecutive numbers in each room, plus spacing rules for duplicates.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers; arrows select the largest adjacent number.
- **Kurodoko** — numbers specify visibility counts.
- **Kurotto** — circle sums of contiguous black cells.
- **Shikaku** — rectangle areas equal numbers.
- **Five Cells** — cell numbers indicate surrounding block lines.
- **Nansuke** — fill blank cells with given numbers from a list; each number is one digit; numbers are arranged vertically or horizontally.
- **Usowan** — numbers count adjacent colored cells, except one wrong number per region.
- **Hashiwokakero** — island numbers indicate bridge counts.

## 6) Symbol-orientation / directional constraint puzzles
These use arrows, directions, or orientation-based rules.

- **Hebi** — snake direction of view and arrow cells constrain visibility and numbers.
- **Nagareru** — loop direction is fixed by arrows; wind changes movement constraints.
- **Sashigane** — arrows point to the bend of an L-shaped block.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move along tracks within countries.
- **Makaro** — arrow cells point to the largest neighboring number.
- **Suraromu** — gates must be crossed in order from an open-numbered starting circle.
- **Yajilin** — arrows indicate how many black cells lie in that direction.
- **Yosenabe** — arrow paths show circle movement into gray areas.

## 7) Shape and pattern puzzles
These focus on shape equality, shape matching, or pattern-based uniqueness.

- **Chained Block** — repeated block shape forbidden within a chain.
- **Double Choco** — paired areas must match in form.
- **Evolomino** — later blocks must grow by one square without rotating/flipping.
- **LITS** — tetromino shapes are central; identical shapes may not touch except at corners.
- **Nuritwin** — each region has two equal-size blocks.
- **Choco Banana** — black and white connected components must not both form rectangles/squares in the wrong way.
- **Shakashaka** — triangle placement reveals a white rectangle/square.
- **Tilepaint** — solution outlines a thing or object via tile coloring.

## 8) Adjacency and non-touching constraint puzzles
These mainly rely on cells or groups not touching orthogonally.

- **Akari** — bulbs illuminate rows/columns; bulbs cannot see each other.
- **Chained Block** — blocks in a chain cannot repeat shapes.
- **Fillomino** — same-sized blocks cannot touch.
- **Hitori** — black cells cannot touch.
- **Kurodoko** — black cells cannot touch.
- **LITS** — same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch except at corners.
- **Masyu** — loop constraints around circles.
- **Nurikabe** — black wall cannot form 2×2 or larger; islands must be separated.
- **Nurimisaki** — no 2×2 same-color group.
- **Nuritwin** — blocks in same region must not touch; no 2×2 fully shaded.
- **Usowan** — colored cells cannot touch; white cells must remain connected.
- **Yajilin** — black cells cannot touch.
- **Shakashaka** — remaining white cells must be one rectangle/square.
- **Heyawake** — painted cells cannot touch; white cells must remain connected.

If you want, I can turn this into a stricter taxonomy table with columns like **Primary mechanism**, **Goal**, **Region-based / line-based / shading-based**, and **Key constraints**.
